newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian rail container transport duty rises 15 pct.
newsitem.headline: Russian rail container transport duty rises 15 pct.

text.p: Russia has eliminated a subsidy that allowed companies exporting refined oil products in containers by rail to pay 15 percent less than the usual rate, the Railways Ministry said on Tuesday.
Dmitry Sharamov, ministry spokesman, said a government order scrapping the privileged tariff came into effect on January 1.
He said that the order covered the transport by rail of all types of products and goods shipped in containers, including, predominantly, refined oil products.

"This means companies exporting refined oil products will now be paying 15 percent more than they have paid in the past," he said, adding that the rule covered container transport on domestic rails within Russia and to other countries.
He did not name the absolute size of the new tariff.
Russia exports some of its refined oil products by rail to outlets in the Baltic countries.
